_comment: Synthetic twin of SETAREH: the real tempo (the detected 128 BPM; the piece counts half-time, 64), first downbeat and five section boundaries, with per-section levels as [mean, p95, max] rounded to 0.05, measured with tools/synth.mjs --twin. events.setareh.line is the one hand-written part: eight windows in which a generated meteor streak is born about every four seconds, so each cut has its rays. There are no snare windows on purpose: the twin's onsets thin a 16th grid at random, so a window at the backbeat rate gives snares 0.1 to 27 s apart and the shutter closes in the wrong place. Without events.setareh.snare the piece falls back to the grid's backbeats, exactly 1.875 s apart, which is where the real snares are on average. There is no vstem either (tools/synth.mjs has no such key), so the pole star's breath reads 0. The cue times (moon, dawn, leave) stay the constants in the source.
